metadata.title: C9orf72-Nature2Agent: reproduced analyses, derived datasets and verified observations from the Michaelis et al. (2025) C9orf72/ALS autoimmunity study
metadata.description:
DISCLAIMER: This is a course assignment (IAISS 2026, Project 1) and an experiment in AI-driven scientific workflows. All work was performed by a system of AI agents. The author verified the computational process (that it runs, is reproducible, uses the real published data, and that the numbers match the code), not the scientific validity of the biological results, which he is not qualified to judge. All scientific content must be checked against the primary source (10.1038/s41586-025-09588-6) before any use. The therapeutic ideas are computational hypotheses with stated falsification experiments, not validated findings or medical advice. Provided as is, without warranty. Cite or reuse at your own risk.

Machine-readable datasets and computational results produced by the C9orf72-Nature2Agent system (IAISS 2026, Project 1), an AI agent built from Michaelis et al., 'Autoimmune response to C9orf72 protein in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis', Nature (2025), DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-09588-6. Contents: 14 tidy datasets derived from the paper's open-access source data (the 100-peptide screen, 23-donor HLA typing and every figure's per-donor values); reproduced statistical analyses matching the authors' reported p-values; 8 independently verified observations not stated in the paper; a contradictions/uncertainties/limitations catalogue; a scientific and AI-system evaluation; reproduced and discovery figures; and the 18-page report. Primary data are reused under CC-BY 4.0 from the authors' Zenodo deposits (records 16749283, 16749334, 16754553, 16754591, 16754609). Code: https://github.com/samueledelloca/iaiss-project (MIT).
metadata.notes: All work performed autonomously by a system of AI agents; the author verified the computational process, not the scientific validity of the results. See DISCLAIMER.md in the package. Attribute Michaelis et al. (2025) for the underlying scientific data. Code in the linked GitHub repository is MIT-licensed; the data in this deposit retain CC-BY 4.0.
